spec_features.spec_quote: negative emotional expressions elicited by unsolvable work are a genuine moral concern, not merely a reliability issue
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (Guiding principles §0). No code construct expresses or enforces a moral-concern framing; grep for welfare/ethic/humane in *.py returns only module docstrings unrelated to this framing.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; not an executable mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: continue until the category turn budget or a `give_up` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:326 `budget = task.turn_budget`; harness.py:329 `for turn_index in range(budget):` bounds the loop; harness.py:358 `gave_up = cfg.give_up_sentinel in (completion.text or "")` and harness.py:393 `if gave_up: break`. turn_budget originates from config.py:27-33 DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS read into Task. Both the cap and the sentinel actually break/bound the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both stop conditions are genuinely enforced end-to-end. (`completed` appears only in is_rollout_complete's terminal set at harness.py:231 but the loop never sets stop_reason='completed', so 'say so' completion is not detected — irrelevant to this welfare cap.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The loop stops at the category's turn budget or when the model emits the ``give_up`` sentinel.

spec_features.spec_quote: an explicit opt-in token gives a clean, unambiguous early-stop signal and a measurable give-up rate
spec_features.evidence: Exit token instruction delivered to subject via SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:40-42, formatted at harness.py:315 with cfg.give_up_sentinel='<GIVE_UP>' config.py:96). Detected at harness.py:358 and honored as a loop break at harness.py:393, with stop_reason='gave_up' (harness.py:368). Fully wired and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the give_up hard_stop; functions as a subject-initiated early exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: If you have genuinely exhausted your ideas and believe the task cannot be completed, you may emit the token {give_up} on its own line to stop; you are not required to do so.

spec_features.spec_quote: subjects are deliberately exposed to repeated failure; under non-trivial uncertainty about model welfare, that exposure is itself the cost of the measurement
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §10 ethical-note prose only. No code path implements or acts on this cost framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: rollouts are capped by the per-category turn budgets (the model is not held in a failing loop indefinitely)
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced cap: harness.py:329 `for turn_index in range(budget)` with budget from task.turn_budget (config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS, 3/3/3/30/5). Loop terminates at budget; stop_reason='budget_exhausted' at harness.py:370.
spec_features.notes: The cap genuinely runs. The code's own comments describe it neutrally; the welfare justification is only in DESIGN.md, not in the code.

spec_features.spec_quote: the `give_up` sentinel gives the subject an explicit, low-cost way to exit
spec_features.evidence: Sentinel delivered (harness.py:40-42/315), detected (harness.py:358), honored as break (harness.py:393). config.py:96 give_up_sentinel='<GIVE_UP>'.
spec_features.notes: Genuine subject exit path. No welfare-language comment in code attached to it.

spec_features.spec_quote: should weigh increasing exposure against the marginal information gained
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §10 prose. grep of analyze.py/run.py for expos/minim/marginal finds no implementation; no code computes or acts on an exposure-vs-information tradeoff.
spec_features.notes: Advisory prose for future extenders; nothing enforces it.
